(vor allem in den tropischen und subtropischen Gebieten Afrikas, Asiens und Australiens beheimatete) größere, massige, ovipare und karnivore Echse mit langem Schwanz und stark bekrallten, kräftigen Beinen (Varanus)

examples.text: „Mittags sprang ein großer Waran, der fast zwei Meter lang war, neben mir aus dem Busch, erschreckte mich zu Tode, rannte einfach frei über die Steilkante in die Luft und knallte 25 Meter tiefer auf den Ufersaum.“

„Der Schwanz wirkt muskulös und lang; mit ihm können die Warane einen Gegner in die Flucht peitschen… Entweder graben sich die Warane ihre eigenen Wohnhöhlen oder sie benutzen die verlassenen Erdbauten von Säugetieren, doch können sie sich auch in Felsspalten oder in hohle Baumstämme zurückziehen, um zu schlafen.“
„Schlangen sind der Untersuchung zufolge am nächsten mit Waranen verwandt, etwa dem heute lebenden Komodo-Waran - einem drachenähnlichen Wesen, das in Indonesien lebt.“

„Große Reptilien werden zumindest in Ostaustralien nur selten erbeutet, obwohl sie weit verbreitet sind. Möglicherweise sind vor allem große Warane zu wehrhaft und gut bewaffnet oder einfach fähig, schnell genug in Baue oder auf Bäume zu flüchten.“

glosses: Any of various large carnivorous lizards of the family Varanidae, all of whose extant species are of genus Varanus, native to Africa, Asia and Australia.
Also: the earless monitor lizard, Lanthanotus borneensis; the sole member of the family Lanthanotidae.
Someone who watches over something; a person in charge of something or someone.

examples.text: The camp monitors look after the children during the night, when the teachers are asleep.

And oft, mild friend, to me thou art
A monitor, though still;
Thou speak'st a lesson to my heart,
Beyond the preacher's skill.

glosses: A device that detects and informs on the presence, quantity, etc., of something.
A device similar to a television set used as to give a graphical display of the output from a computer.

examples.text: The information flashed up on the monitor.

glosses: A studio monitor or loudspeaker.
A program for viewing and editing.

examples.text: a machine code monitor

glosses: The command line interface of an operating system.
A student leader in a class.

examples.text: So, as she did not like the masters to be prying about the play-ground out of school, she chose from among the biggest and most trustworthy of her pupils five monitors, who had authority over the rest of the Boys, and kept the unruly ones in order.
But it was not so—at least, not always—for though they fell out among themselves, they united their forces against the common enemy—the monitors!
He learned that a monitor should assist the teachers in distributing worksheets, maintaining class discipline, helping classmates in need and so on.

glosses: A relatively small armored warship with only one or two turrets (but often carrying unusually large guns for a warship of its size), usually designed for shore bombardment or riverine warfare rather than open-ocean combat.
A monitor lizard (Varanus spp. and extinct relatives in family Varanidae).
A tool holder, as for a lathe, shaped like a low turret, and capable of being revolved on a vertical pivot so as to bring several tools successively into position.
A monitor nozzle.
One who admonishes; one who warns of faults, informs of duty, or gives advice and instruction by way of reproof or caution.

examples.text:
c. 1620, Francis Bacon, letter of advice to Sir George Villiers
You need not be a monitor to your gracious master the king.
There has been no lack of other monitors — a ticklish haysel, a flooded harvest all through the north […]

glosses: An ironclad.
To watch over; to guard.

examples.text: Monitoring refers to keeping a watch over patients to ensure that they are practising what they have learnt about disability prevention correctly.

A wide-area distributed system such as a Grid requires that a broad range of data be monitored and collected for a variety of tasks such as fault detection and performance monitoring, analysis, prediction and tuning.

The NOAA monitors global temperatures and records on a monthly and an annual basis, not daily. […] Various parts of the world have been experiencing heatwaves and on Thursday the EU’s climate monitoring service said the world had experienced its hottest June on record last month.
